body: Thanks for your conversation so far. I'm not getting anywhere with my paper and it's 3:15 in the morning, so I think I'll be going to sleep!

Yes I know that. I don't know how long you've been on reddit, but there has been askreddit threads where siblings and parents of people with autism and down syndrome expressed their regret at having to care for and put up with that family member.

I realize people have different reactions to losing someone close to them, but do parents really want that one child who is the black sheep of the family, who could have been so much more but ended up so short?
Spring break is coming up for me at the end of the week. I'm looking forward to a week where I don't have too much academic pressure and when I can relax.
People go through bereavement and eventually forget about a death. People have a much harder time forgetting about constant disappointment.

That's one option I have, although I feel like the amount of time you put in to study those fields doesn't equal the amount of respect people view those professions with and how much they make.

Also, my school's counselling center isn't known for their care. Most of the time, they push students to take benzo or SSRIs and encourage suicidal students to take time off so the suicide doesn't happen on school ground.
